Description: Though Jerusalem is not specifically mentioned, had there been a great earthquake (which we believe that occurred), Jerusalem was damaged. BM5 and AUS assign an intensity of VIII and IX, respectively. AM and GCT, based on Josephus and Nathan HaBavli, note that Jerusalem was hit in Ein-Rogel (landslides), the Temple, Valley of Hinnom (landslides) and perhaps Olive Mt.
AM (p.96) and KA2 question the entry in BM5 concerning the reliability of this event and elaborate the sequence of sources leading to a potential spurious event.
AM ollowing the Babylonian Talmud. Baba Kama: "earthquake struck Israel and the land trembled a hundred miles in all directions". KA2 questions and event that hit Jerusalem
The testimony of St. Mathwre is not clear and one could not conclude for sure that Jerusalem has been hit.

Although it is possible that Jerusalem sustained some damage, the sources do not refer to it. They do describe at some length the repairable and irreparable damage caused to the Aksa mosque around its mihrab, but details about damage to other buildings and houses in Jerusalem are lacking (AM aftter Theoph. 422; al-Dhah. Tar. Islam v. 39–40).
Jerusalem / al Aqsa Mousqe: The Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem was allegedly damaged but no source (and there are only secondary sources) mentions an earthquake
damage: al Aqsa Mousqe, Dome of the rock, Mihrab of Dawud, David Citadel
damage: part of the minaret over the Zawiya al-Darkah, dome near the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
Three shocks were felt in Jerusalem
damage: Holy tomb, Walls, Tower of the Temple, gate of Mercy, Yishmael mosque, al-Aqsa, Church of the Holy Sepulchre, the Ashrafiyya, the Aminiyya, Fakhriyya, Olive Mountain
damage: Holy Sepulchre, Greek and Armenean Churchs
Houses suffered various degrees of damage without loss of life

In Jerusalem the earthquake was not very strong and caused only limited damage. It is alleged that the minarets of the mosque at Kafr al-Tur, east of the city, were shaken down (AM after Calman 1837; Neman 1837).
Slight tremor in Jerusalem (Royal Commision on Historical Manuscripts, 1975. Report on the papers of the Palestine Exploration Fund: Western Survey 1871-1902, 10)

In the report of the Royal Commision on Historical Manuscripts from 1975 on the PEF western survey there is a report of  ""a small earthquake tremor in J. “[Jerusalem, my interpretation] . No other reporting source at the time but the British reports tend to be highy reliable.
Amiran et al (1994): foreshock 21:00-21:30, MMS III. Three main shocks, 23:05, direction north to south. Mount of Olives: MMS VII. Aftershock 03:00, MMS III.
